comments.quote_zh: Dan Olson（又名 Folding Ideas）关于这个话题的一部很棒的纪录片
comments.text_zh: 对很大一群人来说，相信地平说绝对不是玩笑（不过对更大一群人来说，它绝对是个笑话）。它属于一个更广泛的运动，涉及圣经字面主义和阴谋论，描述一场国际性的反基督教阴谋。容易被证伪这件事，对这类阴谋论来说其实不算什么问题。它实际上有点像成员的一种纯度测试。就像骗局至今还在用“尼日利亚王子”的套路，因为这能确保只有最有希望上钩的目标才会中招。Dan Olson（又名 Folding Ideas）关于这个话题的一部很棒的纪录片：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Belief in Flat Earth is most definitely not a joke for a very large group of people (though it is absolutely a joke for a much larger group of people). It is part of a wider movement of biblical literalism and conspiracy theories describing an international anti-christian plot. The fact that it is easily disproved isn't really a problem for these kinds of conspiracy theories. It actually kind of acts as a purity test for members. Kind of like how scams still use the "nigerian prince" trope, because it ensures only the most promising marks fall for it. A great documentary on the topic by Dan Olson aka Folding ideas: [VIDEO]

comments.author: jiggawatts
comments.story_title: Interesting
comments.why_zh: 荒诞信仰作为群体内部暗号
comments.quote_zh: 我看过的关于整件事最好的分析之一
comments.text_zh: 我看过的关于整件事最好的分析之一，是 Folding Ideas 的《In Search Of A Flat Earth》：[VIDEO] 本质上，宣称荒诞的信仰是一种暗号，用来表明自己属于群体内部。荒诞本身就是重点，因为这把他们和局外人区分开来。正常人一直都会说真实或符合事实的话，那可不是好的区分标志！这些说法必须是假的/或荒诞的，才能发挥其预期作用。与主流宗教相比，地平说神话甚至都没那么离谱，而且完全属于邪教用来识别内部成员的那类信仰的同一范畴。Scientology 就是个例子，但还有很多其他例子。我强烈建议看完整段视频，因为这一现象远比我最初以为的复杂得多。
comments.text: One of the best analyses of this whole thing I've seen is "In Search Of A Flat Earth" by Folding Ideas: [VIDEO] Essentially, professing absurd beliefs is a sort of shibboleth to demonstrate in-group membership. The absurdity is the point , because it differentiates them from outsiders. Normal people make true or factual statements all the time, that's not a good differentiator! The statements need to be false and/or absurd to function for their intended purpose. The Flat Earth mythos isn't even that outlandish compared to mainstream religions, and well within the same wheelhouse as the type of beliefs used to identify the in-group in cults. Scientology comes to mind, but there are many others. I highly recommend watching the entire video, because there is a lot more to the phenomena than I initially suspected.

comments.why_zh: 深入探讨人们为何加入 Flat Earth 这类社群
comments.quote_zh: Folding Ideas 的 Dan Olsen 做过一个很棒的视频 [1]，作为一次深度剖析
comments.text_zh: > 吸引人的不是 FE，而是这些人非常不看重社会从众，因此能以“合群的人”做不到的方式保持诚实。Folding Ideas 的 Dan Olsen 做过一个很棒的视频 [1]，深入探讨了 Flat Earth 社群以及它如何存续下来。TL;DW（不过真的值得一看）是：人们既想要也需要社群，而所有社群都有表明你属于它们的方式。有时是语言，有时是衣着，有时是行为——这些“资格”因群体而千差万别，但在很多情况下，从外部看，一个群体表现出的行为（例如相信地球是平的）与人们对该个体其余方面的认知（例如具备科学素养）对不上，直到你把“这些行为除了确保群体成员身份之外并不重要”这一点考虑进去。用这个视角看，很多事情对我来说就合理多了，包括许多有组织的宗教。人们只是想有归属感，而且通常“入门代价”与归属某处的回报相比微不足道。谢谢你分享你的故事。它帮助我理解了其中一些事情的“为什么”，也让我觉得自己与其他人更有连接。[1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: > It's not the FE that's attractive, it's that they're people who put very little value on social conformity and thus can be honest in a way that "fit ins" can't. There's a marvelous video [1] that Dan Olsen of Folding Ideas did as a deep dive into the community of Flat Earth and how it manages to survive. The TL;DW (though it really is worth the watch) is that people both want and need community, and all communities have ways of signaling that you belong to them. Sometimes it's language, sometimes it's clothes, sometimes it's behaviors--the "qualifications" vary wildly by group, but in many cases from the outside the exhibited behaviors of a group (e.g., believing in flat earth) don't jive with the rest of the perceived individual (e.g., scientifically literate) until you factor in that the behaviors don't have to matter beyond ensuring membership to a group. A whole lot of things make a lot more sense to me when seen through that lens, including a lot of organized religion. People just want to belong, and often the "price of entry" is inconsequential vs. the payoff of belonging somewhere. Thanks for sharing your story. It helps me to understand the "Why" of some of these things, and helps me feel more connected to my fellow beings. [1]: [VIDEO]

If you then carefully lower the camera to the ground, you can watch objects (boats! people! small buildings!) dissapear behind the curvature of the lake's surface. Dan Olson ("Folding Ideas") demonstrates this experiment in the video[1] I recommended in an earlier post[2]. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]

comments.text_zh: 所以，正如你指出的，YouTube 封禁内容的二阶效应很有趣，也很难预测。问题是，对二阶效应的恐惧是否应该阻止 YouTube 为达成期望的一阶效应而采取行动？提供一些背景：在 YouTube 改变算法之前，地平说视频基本上创造了现代地平说运动 [1]。这种效应很可能也能朝相反方向起作用。我倾向于认为，当人们在社交上联系良好时，不太会被阴谋论等吸引。疫情的问题在于存在一个负反馈循环：因为存在致命病毒，我们才有这些社交隔离限制；而病毒一直未受控制的一个原因，部分在于一小部分被社会隔离的人被错误信息吸引。[1] 更多细节见纪录片 In Search of A Flat Earth：[VIDEO]
comments.text: So the second-order effects of YouTube banning content, as you point out, are interesting and hard to predict. The question is should fear of second order effects prevent YouTube from taking action towards a desired first order effect? For some context, prior to Youtube changing the algorithm, flat earth videos basically created the modern flat earth movement [1]. It's likely that this effect can go the other way, too. I like to think that people are less drawn to conspiracy theories etc. when they are socially well-connected. The trouble about the pandemic is that there is a negative feedback loop: we have these socially isolating restrictions because there is a deadly virus, and one reason the virus remains unchecked is, in part because a subset of socially isolated people are drawn to misinformation. [1] See the documentary In Search of A Flat Earth for more details: [VIDEO]

comments.author: WillDaSilva
comments.story_title: Why “Trusting the Science” Is Complicated
comments.text_zh: 人们因持有错误信念而造成的伤害有时相当复杂，但仍然极其重要且影响深远。尤其对于地平说者，这段视频揭示了一点：为什么他们的思维方式是有害的：[VIDEO] 极其简化地说，允许错误信念进入一个人的信念网络会腐蚀它。这通常会导致大量其他错误信念。地平说者几乎从不只相信一个明显错误的阴谋论。他们在认识上变得易受影响，更糟的是，他们往往满怀热情地传播这些糟糕的思维方式。在更一般的情况下，我建议你了解信念伦理。斯坦福哲学百科全书关于该主题的页面是个不错的起点：[LINK] 也许有人能来以更简洁但同样（或理想情况下更）令人信服的方式回答你的问题。而让你花几个小时自我教育，这个请求已经是我目前能给出的最好办法了。
comments.text: The harm people cause by holding believing false beliefs is rather complicated at times, yet extremely important and impactful nonetheless. For flat earthers in particular this video sheds some light on why their way of thinking is harmful: [VIDEO] To be extremely reductive, allowing false beliefs into one's web of beliefs corrupts it. This typically gives rise to a multitude of other false beliefs. Flat earthers almost never only believe one obviously false conspiracy theory. They become epistemically susceptible, and worse still, they tend to spread these awful ways of thinking with great zeal. In the more general case, I recommend you learn about the ethics of belief. The Standford Encyclopedia of Philosophy page on the topic is a good starting point: [LINK] Maybe someone can come along and answer your question in a more succinct yet equally (or ideally more) convincing way. This request that you commit several hours to educating yourself is the best I can do at this time.

comments.text_zh: 我猜你发的链接会是这个：[VIDEO]（Folding Ideas，“In Search of a Flat Earth”）。他认真对待了他们关于在一个非常大的湖上做某些实验时会看到什么的两三个说法，亲自尝试，看到了如果地球是曲面就会预期的结果，并把结果发到某个 flat earth 社区论坛；当他们提出他可能哪里搞砸了时，他改进实验，并继续发现曲率（显然）。真正的故事在于，他们如何回应完全按照他们的方式给出的反面证据，以及那个社群四年前正走向何方（注意——我猜——那部分也必然变得“政治化”）。[EDIT] 我想我把这个网站会感兴趣的重点埋没了：视频花了相当多时间讲 YouTube 的“算法”如何把 Flat Earth 视频的一点小成功当作线索，主动把它们大力推给算法认为可能喜欢这类内容的人（那些容易掉进这个特定兔子洞的人——这远不只是“相信地球是平的”这一个具体信念），但现在 flat earth 正在衰退，因为那个算法和其他“算法”开始把同样这些人送去……Q-anon 内容。顺便说一句，几年前有一部规模还算大的关于 Flat Earth 的纪录片，里面有来自一次 flat earth 大会的一些人尝试与这个视频里描绘的非常相似的实验（涉及跨越一个大湖的物体可见性），结果也可想而知
comments.text: I figured your link would be this one: [VIDEO] (Folding Ideas, "In Search of a Flat Earth") He takes a couple of their claims seriously about what one will see when attempting particular experiments involving a very large lake, attempts them, sees the results one would expect if the Earth were curved, and reports this to some flat earth community forum, refining the experiment as they suggest ways he may have screwed it up, and continuing to find curvature (obviously). The real story is how they react to contrary evidence delivered entirely on their terms, and where that community was heading four years ago (beware—I guess—that part also becomes necessarily "political"). [EDIT] I guess I buried the lede for this site's interest, which is that the video devotes a fair bit of time to how the Youtube "algorithm" took a little success for Flat Earth videos as a cue to aggressively promote them to people it identified as maybe liking them (those inclined to fall down that particular rabbit hole—which involves a lot more than just the specific belief that the earth is flat), but now flat earth is in decline, because that and other "algorithms" started sending the same folks to... Q-anon content instead. comments.text_zh: 我最初探究这个假说时，留下的感受是：最好的概括是，这是一个学术上有争议的领域，双方都有可信度，哪一方都不能被准确地视为边缘或主流——这与你最初的评论相反。你说的一切都没有动摇这个看法，而我也没有任何相关的科学专业知识可以拿来支持某一方。对于哪一方证据更好、我更愿意在概率上倾向哪一方，我有自己的个人看法，但这个看法究竟是什么，最终并不重要。话虽如此，有一件事在我读你第一条评论时让我略感不安，而你后来的评论只是加深了我的这一印象。你似乎是从一种传教式的、而非科学的角度来看待这个话题：存在一个核心信念，需要尽可能传播给更多人，而任何挑战这一信念的东西都需要被迅速清除。你的措辞——"尼安德特人"、"地质学的黑眼圈"——对你的论证没有帮助。我提这个，只是因为周末我看了一个视频[1]，讨论的是地平说信徒以及他们使用的一些论证风格，回想起来，你的评论与之相似得令人吃惊，只不过是在一个可接受的观念上，而不是一个荒唐的想法上。[1] [视频]
comments.text: When I first poked at this hypothesis, I came away feeling that the best characterization was that it's an area of academic dispute where both sides have credibility and neither side can be accurately considered fringe or mainstream, in contrast to your initial comment. Nothing you have said has shaken that belief, and I have no relevant scientific expertise to offer in support of one side or the other. I have my personal opinion on which side I feel has the better evidence and prefer on the balance of probabilities, but what that opinion is is ultimately unimportant. That said, there is one thing that mildly concerned me when I read your first comment and that your later comments have only reinforced my impressions. You seem to be approaching this topic from an evangelical perspective, and not a scientific one: that there is a core belief, this needs to be disseminated to as many people as possible, and that anything that challenges that belief needs to be swiftly eliminated. Your rhetoric--"Neanderthal", "black eye for geology"--does not help your argument. I only bring this up because I saw a video over the weekend [1] discussing Flat Earthers and some of the argumentation style they used, and on reflection, it was striking how similar your comments were, just on an acceptable opinion rather than a loony idea. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 地平说信徒转向了 QAnon
comments.quote_zh: 它死了，是因为地平说信徒已经转向了 QAnon [1]。
comments.text_zh: QAnon 本身没有任何天然的病毒式传播特质，QAnon 的理论没有什么真正的道理，而且一半时间它们自相矛盾。QAnon 只是一种唯我论式、不加批判、妄想性思维的最新变种，这种思维早在互联网之前就存在，也将在互联网消亡很久之后继续存在。想知道地平说理论后来怎么样了吗？它曾经是那个时代的"病毒式"坏主意，但你现在环顾四周，它基本已经死了。它死了，是因为地平说信徒已经转向了 QAnon [1]。"富有的民主党人喝儿童的血"字面上就是一个随机的愚蠢想法，它之所以传播，只是因为这群白痴彼此都在说话。它可以换成任何东西；在另一个十年，他们谈论的会是共济会，或者地平说，或者犹太人议程。共同的主题不是那个想法或政治，而是那种破碎的心态，它造出一个世界观：什么都不怪你，所有坏事都是非人的他者造成的，而你是少数聪明到能看见别人看不见的东西的人。以为审查这些人真能解决什么问题，那是愚蠢的。因为你从来没有解决最初吸引他们走向这些垃圾的破碎心理，他们会继续寻找其他出口，而你试图审查他们只会进一步喂养他们的妄想。审查也许能帮你在互联网上避开他们，但看看你能不能也在投票站避开他们。[1] In Search Of A Flat Earth [视频]
comments.text: Nothing about QAnon is inherently viral, there's no real rhyme or reason to QAnon theories and they contradict each other half the time. QAnon is just the latest adaptation of solipsistic, uncritical, and delusional thinking that started long before the internet and will continue long after it dies. Ever wonder what happened to flat earth theory? That used to be the "viral" bad idea of the time, but if you look around now it's practically dead. It's dead because flat earthers have moved on to QAnon [1]. "Wealthy democrats drink the blood of children" is literally a random stupid idea that only spreads because these idiots all talk to each other. It could be anything; In a different decade they would instead be talking about the Freemasons, or a flat earth, or the Jewish agenda. The common theme is not the idea or the politics, it's the broken mentality that creates a worldview in which nothing is your fault, everything bad is caused by inhuman others, and you are one of the few smart enough to see what others cannot. It's foolish to think that censoring these people actually solves anything. Because you never addressed the broken psychology that attracts them to this garbage in the first place, they'll continue finding other outlets, your attempts to censor them only feeding their delusions further. Censorship might help you avoid them on the internet, but let's see if you can avoid them at the polls. [1] In Search Of A Flat Earth [VIDEO]
